If we let $u=x-1,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-1$ | $1$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{5}^{x-1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{5}^{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{5}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}({5}^{1}-{5}^{-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(5-\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{24}{5\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\end{aligned}
$$
